history.period: 16th century CE (older antiquity claimed by legend)
history.summary: CONFIRMED IDENTITY: the row is the Kasi Viswanathar Temple at Kumbakonam, on the northern bank of the Mahamaham tank (about 1 km from the Kumbakonam bus terminal). This is one of the 12 Shiva temples connected with the Mahamaham festival held every 12 years, and one of the three Kayarohana stalams of Tamil Nadu (with Kanchikkaronam and Naagaikkaronam) - a shrine where all beings become one with Shiva during the great deluge. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, the 28th in the series of Tevara stalams in the Chola kingdom south of the Kaveri. The moolavar is Kasi Viswanathar with Visalakshi Amman; the Nava Kannigas (Ganga, Yamuna, Narmada, Saraswati, Kaveri, Godavari, Tungabhatra, Krishna and Sarayu) are enshrined here, since the nine rivers are believed to assemble in the Mahamaham tank during the festival. Legends: Rama and Lakshmana worshipped Shiva here during their search for Sita and acquired Rudramsam to fight Ravana (some accounts name Ravana as the installer of the lingam); Viswanathar of Kasi is believed to have manifested himself here at Kudanthai Karonam after the nine sacred rivers prayed to him at Banaras. The 2-acre complex has two gopurams, the western tower rising 72 ft in seven tiers. The present masonry structure was built under the Nayaks in the 16th century; administered by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department of Tamil Nadu. name: Kasi Viswanathar Temple
town_description: Kumbakonam, in Thanjavur district on the Cauvery river about 40 km from Thanjavur and 273 km from Chennai, is a historic temple town famed for its Mahamaham festival (held every 12 years) and dense cluster of Shaivite and Vaishnavite shrines.

travel.airport: Tiruchirappalli International Airport (TRZ), about 100 km away, is the nearest airport.
travel.railway: Kumbakonam Junction (KMU) on the Chennai-Tiruchirapalli line; the temple is about 1 km from the Kumbakonam bus terminal, walkable, with town and mini buses stopping at Mahamaham Tank.
travel.road: Well connected by road to Chennai, Tiruchirappalli, Thanjavur and other south Indian cities; the temple is beside the Mahamaham tank in central Kumbakonam.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; February-March for Masi Magam. The Mahamaham festival occurs once every 12 years, when lakhs of devotees gather.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:30 PM and 4:00-8:30 PM (per wanderlog); six daily rituals run from 6:00 AM to about 9:00 PM (per Wikipedia) - verify before visiting.
